runtime_dependency_pins.vllm is null: the docs publish no == version for the vLLM stack and delegate to `paddleocr install_genai_server_deps vllm`. The build freezes pip inside the image and records pip_freeze_sha256 (masterplan section 38); the canary records the resolved version.

inference_config.layout_detection_model_name and layout_detection_model_dir are null: the PaddleOCR-VL pipeline resolves its own default layout model and the official docs name no revision for it. The canary must record the resolved layout model files and their sha256 from the built image, not guess them here.

paddleocr_version_finding.resolution: Preference-order option (1): the official image is used unmodified. No paddleocr or paddlex version is installed over it. The build and the bootstrap assert the image carries paddleocr 3.6.0 / paddlex 3.6.1 and fail closed otherwise, then add only what the official docs say that image still needs for the vLLM genai server (the prebuilt FlashAttention 2.8.2 wheel, because the image ships no nvcc, and `paddleocr install_genai_server_deps vllm`) plus huggingface_hub for the arena's own pinned weight fetch.
paddleocr_version_finding.residual_risk: `paddleocr install_genai_server_deps vllm` is a vendor-resolved install with no published == versions, so it may still move paddlex or transformers inside the image. It is asserted before, not after; the resolved set is captured in the image pip freeze and the bootstrap receipt, and the canary records it.

framework_floor_audit.required: paddleocr[doc-parser] >= 3.6.0 and paddlepaddle >= 3.2.1 (model card); the genai_server's vLLM must register PaddleOCRVLForConditionalGeneration, which upstream vllm v0.17.1's registry.py does
framework_floor_audit.image_ships: paddleocr 3.6.0 / paddlex 3.6.1 / paddlepaddle-gpu 3.2.1, from the image config label org.opencontainers.image.version=0006f78-ppocr3.6-pdx3.6 (D43); the genai_server's vLLM version is unknown from evidence because it is installed at boot by `paddleocr install_genai_server_deps vllm`, so the preflight reads it at run time instead of guessing
framework_floor_audit.action: no pin added - D43 settled that the official image is the vendor path and nothing is installed over it. bootstrap.sh gains an architecture preflight that resolves PaddleOCRVL through the toolkit and asks the genai_server's vLLM registry for the checkpoint's architecture before the server starts.

cuda_floor.source: max(base image CUDA runtime, the CUDA-tagged wheel this runtime installs itself)

observed.CUDA_VERSION: absent: the image config declares no CUDA env at all (it is a python:3.10 base)
observed.NVIDIA_REQUIRE_CUDA: absent: the image config declares no CUDA env at all (it is a python:3.10 base)

cuda_floor.vendor_documented_floor: none published: the vendor documents no driver floor beyond the image's own CUDA runtime
cuda_floor.why_not_12_6: The image is a python:3.10 base with no CUDA env at all: its CUDA runtime is whatever paddlepaddle-gpu was built against, and the config history names the cu126 index. This runtime then installs a flash-attn wheel built for cu128, in both bootstrap.sh and the Dockerfile, so the process loads CUDA 12.8 binaries. 12.8 is the higher of the two floors; 12.6 would repeat the incident with a different library.
cuda_floor.rationale: min_cuda_version is the lowest CUDA version a RunPod host may report for this runtime to start. It is sent as the create payload's allowedCudaVersions -- every version RunPod lists at or above it -- because pod 3xag0y00rgoj4n ran this campaign's CUDA 12.9 image on a host reporting cudaVersion 12.8 and died in torch._C._cuda_init with CUDA error 804 after the pod was already billing. Read anonymously from the pinned image's own OCI config blob at the digest runtime.json pins; nothing is inferred from the image name.
